title: AWS Sign-In now supports OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with AWS Sign-In now supports OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
body_markdown:
AWS Sign-In now supports OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693), enabling applications to exchange third-party OpenID Connect (OIDC) tokens for short-lived, AWS service-scoped OAuth access tokens. This allows customers to securely integrate third-party applications with supported AWS services without sharing AWS credentials, while maintaining access controls through AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).


This capability is available for supported[AWS services that use AWS Sign-In OAuth](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/signin/latest/userguide/oauth-services-supporting.html) , enabling customers to use existing identity providers to securely access AWS services without managing additional credentials.


**To learn more** , see the[AWS Sign-In User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/signin/latest/userguide/oauth-sign-in-overview.html#oauth-sign-in-authorization-models) ,[AWS MCP Server User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/signin/latest/userguide/aws-mcp-server.html#aws-mcp-server-auth-models) and the[AWS Glue launch announcement](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/10/glue-catalog-oauth-iceberg-rest/) .
